They have the lowest roster stability over the past three years of any team in the league. It is the main reason they fell from No. 3 in FPR in 2023 to No. 22 this season. They're at least still young, projected as the fourth-youngest roster this season. -- Oliver

Bold prediction for 2027-29: Boozer will challenge Pau Gasol as the most productive rookie in Grizzlies history. In 2001-02, Gasol won Rookie of the Year honors by averaging 17.6 points, 8.9 rebounds and 2.1 blocks for a 23-win Memphis team. Boozer is replacing Morant -- another Rookie of the Year winner -- as the rebuilding Grizzlies' franchise player, so he should enjoy a large role from day one. What's more, the 19-year-old forward has the size and physicality to make an immediate impact. While Gasol's 7.6 win shares as a rookie will be hard to top, Boozer led the NCAA in that metric as a Duke freshman. -- Golliver

Previous ranking: 17

23. Washington Wizards

Three-year outlook: The Wizards could have jumped up higher in these rankings, after adding Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa since last year's edition. But the Wizards still don't project as a playoff team in the East this season, and then Davis could reach free agency, so caution is still warranted when anticipating just how much Washington might improve after its infusion of star power. -- Kram

Roster question looming: Until an extension is signed, the future of Davis is the big question hanging over the organization. Eligible to sign up to a four-year, $275 million extension since Aug. 6, Davis and Washington have elected to table talks until the regular season. On the court, there were questions on building winning habits despite the addition of Young, Davis and Dybantsa. Last season, the Wizards won consecutive games only four times with no win streaks of three or more games. -- Marks

FPR nugget to know: Over their past three seasons of failure, the Wizards have ranked either 29th or 30th in FPR's player ratings. At the same time, their overall FPR ranking was in the bottom five, so the other factors weren't making up ground. The personnel grade rose to No. 23 this year, largely due to lottery luck and finally sacrificed some of their cash advantage (second across the past three years in money) to acquire Davis and Young. -- Oliver

Bold prediction for 2027-29: Young will surpass the Wizards' franchise record of 11.7 assists per game set by Russell Westbrook in 2020-21. After signing a $212 million contract extension this summer, Young said he looked forward to sharing the scoring load with Davis and a growing cast of recent first-round picks that includes Dybantsa, Alex Sarr and Kyshawn George. For the Wizards to accomplish their developmental goals, Young must shift into a pass-first mode and tighten up his shot selection. Picture James Harden during his stint with the Philadelphia 76ers. -- Golliver

Previous ranking: 26

24. Brooklyn Nets

Three-year outlook: Like the Grizzlies, the Nets rank near the top of both the draft and money categories. But beyond the frontcourt pairing of Michael Porter Jr. and new Net Julius Randle, this is still a roster devoid of win-now talent, as Brooklyn is still primarily focused on the development of a half-dozen recent first-round picks. That timeline means it's hard to expect too many wins from this team in the near term. -- Kram

Roster question looming: Besides the internal development of a league-high eight players on first-round rookie contracts, there are questions on the future of Porter. After averaging a career high 24.2 points per game last season, Porter is in the final year of his contract and eligible to sign a four-year extension. The decision will play a significant role in the Nets' flexibility next summer. -- Marks

FPR nugget to know: The Nets are top five in both money and draft for the third straight season but bottom five in players. Usually, teams in that situation are two years away from being about average or better. But given Brooklyn's low win predictions for this season, the franchise might have actually been two years away from being two years away back in 2024 (to paraphrase Fran Fraschilla). -- Oliver

Bold prediction for 2027-29: The NBA's lottery reform will expose Brooklyn's lack of top-end talent and cripple its hopes of building primarily through the draft. In turn, the Nets will get bored of rebuilding and make an all-in play for a superstar during one of the next two summers. This is just the natural life cycle for Brooklyn, which sold the farm for Kevin Garnett and Paul Pierce in 2013 and landed Kevin Durant and Kyrie Irving in 2019. -- Golliver

Previous ranking: 27

25. Phoenix Suns

Three-year outlook: Phoenix is out of the Future Power Rankings basement after a surprising playoff berth. But the Suns' broader future doesn't look all that different now, featuring financial issues -- especially if they extend Miles Bridges -- and a barren draft cupboard, after they traded yet another unprotected first-rounder for Bridges this summer. -- Kram

Roster question looming: Since buying the team in 2023, Mat Ishbia has paid $270 million in tax penalties the past four seasons. After taking a hiatus in 2025-26, the Suns are projected to pay over $40 million this season. A possible extension for Bridges will only increase the Suns' tax burden in the future. Not including Bridges, Phoenix is $13 million below the threshold next season. -- Marks

FPR nugget to know: The Suns have ranked in the bottom six in the draft category for four straight years. That coincides quite well with their acquisitions of Kevin Durant and Bradley Beal for a collection of draft picks and swaps. Those deals compromised these assets across the next three years. -- Oliver

Bold prediction for 2027-29: Khaman Maluach is Phoenix's best hope of escaping the treadmill of mediocrity. After giving up on the Devin Booker and Durant pairing, the Suns have constructed a low-ceiling roster with veterans such as Dillon Brooks and Bridges. How does Booker, who turns 30 in October, ever get back to making noise in the playoffs? Phoenix doesn't have much in the way of young talent besides the 19-year-old Maluach, a 2025 lottery pick who played sparingly as a rookie. Still, the South Sudanese center has a massive 7-foot-1 frame and flashed 3-point range at the Las Vegas Summer League. Phoenix really needs Maluach to hit or it risks squandering the rest of Booker's prime. -- Golliver

Previous ranking: 30

26. New Orleans Pelicans

Three-year outlook: New Orleans was already bad last season, with a 26-56 record, and the team's current brain trust hasn't inspired much confidence with its moves (or lack thereof) since coming to power. Add in the worst market situation in the league, and New Orleans might be stuck near the bottom of these rankings for a while yet. -- Kram

Roster question looming: Unlike last season, New Orleans controls its first-round pick in 2027. The unknown is how the same returning roster that won 26 games, responds to a new head coach in Jamahl Mosley. President of basketball operations Joe Dumars and Mosley have to evaluate the upside of the roster when healthy, or whether time has run out and change is needed. Fourteen players are under contract for 2027-28, including Zion Williamson, Dejounte Murray, Herbert Jones and Trey Murphy III. -- Marks

FPR nugget to know: The Pelicans are tied for the worst rating in management. When looking at the bottom-five scores, the average three-year win percentage of those teams has been 38%, the equivalent of a 31-win season. (There were a handful of teams that actually got above 50%, but not many.) -- Oliver

Bold prediction for 2027-29: The Zion era will end with little fanfare. More than seven years have passed since the Pelicans won the 2019 lottery and selected Williamson with the top pick. New Orleans has little to show for its good fortune: Williamson has played fewer than 40 games per season while dealing with multiple injuries, and he has yet to make his playoff debut. Williamson's contract is set to expire after the 2027-28 season, and New Orleans has already started accumulating its next wave of young prospects to carry the franchise into the future. Whether New Orleans trades Williamson or he eventually departs in free agency, his exit will unfortunately be a blip on the national radar. -- Golliver

Previous ranking: 29

27. Chicago Bulls

Three-year outlook: The Bulls' long-awaited rebuild is finally underway, so even though they're not expected to win many games over the next few seasons, at least those losses will come as part of a plan. Chicago hopes that its clean cap and appealing market can aid a turnaround once the time is right to try contending again. -- Kram

Roster question looming: Fair or unfair, the development of rookie Caleb Wilson could play a role not only with the results on the court but whether Chicago becomes a desirable location for trade candidates and free agents. For a team rebuilding, Chicago ranks in the top 10 in three categories: market, money and draft. -- Marks

FPR nugget to know: The Bulls have been the most consistent team in the Future Power Rankings the past four seasons, including this one. Unfortunately, that consistency has been in the bottom range of the rankings. -- Oliver

Bold prediction for 2027-29: Wilson will rank in the NBA's top 10 jersey sales by 2030. Despite a classic red uniform and lasting global popularity that dates to Michael Jordan's heyday, the Bulls haven't had a merchandise powerhouse since Derrick Rose. Wilson's high-flying game and boundless confidence will change that. -- Golliver

Previous ranking: 28

28. Milwaukee Bucks

Three-year outlook: After trading Giannis Antetokounmpo, Milwaukee is embarking on its first rebuild in more than a decade. But unfortunately for the Bucks, they don't control any of their first-round picks in 2027, 2028, 2029 or 2030, so they'll have to hope for internal development from players already on the roster to eventually push back up the standings. -- Kram

Roster question looming: The Bucks added multiple first-round picks in the Antetokounmpo trade, but those assets do not come to fruition until 2031 and 2033. And though the deal has brought clarity to the future, there are still questions with the roster. Tyler Herro, who is entering the final year of his contract, is extension-eligible. And could Myles Turner or Kyle Kuzma be the next veteran to be traded this season? -- Marks

FPR nugget to know: The market score is the smallest component of the overall rankings and it changes the least from year to year. That being said, the Bucks' score fell this year to its lowest level, No. 27, since peaking in 2019. The decline is a reflection of Antetokounmpo not wanting to stay there, perhaps mixed with snow that you see on the sidewalks in February. -- Oliver

Bold prediction for 2027-29: None of the Bucks' opening night starters in 2026 will still be their opening night starters in 2029. Moving on from Antetokounmpo will be a multiyear proposition, and Milwaukee will spend what figures to be a challenging 2026-27 season sifting through its roster to identify potential keepers. Outside of Ryan Rollins and 2026 lottery picks Brayden Burries and Nate Ament, Milwaukee is largely lacking in intriguing young talent. -- Golliver

Previous ranking: 21

29. LA Clippers

Three-year outlook: Here's a behind-the-scenes detail of how these rankings came together: The Clippers ranked a half-dozen spots higher before the NBA handed down a draconian punishment for cap circumvention. Now they're second to last, despite a more talented roster than many of the other teams around them, because the Clippers' management, draft and market scores took such a big hit. -- Kram

Roster question looming: Who is in charge? The NBA suspended owner Steve Ballmer for one season and head of basketball operations Lawrence Frank six months. The suspension for Frank carries past the February trade deadline. With no picks at their disposal to trade, the Clippers could be in a holding position until next summer. -- Marks

FPR nugget to know: The Nets of 2018 had money, a good market and draft picks. They chose to use their picks and money to acquire Kevin Durant and Kyrie Irving in a push to get good fast. Until the Kawhi Leonard verdict came down, the Clippers were in a very similar situation, with money, market and picks. That Brooklyn team at least had a couple of good-not-great years before going all-in on a rebuild, but most teams didn't improve quickly. And now the Clippers have a lot fewer picks. -- Oliver

Bold prediction for 2027-29: The Clippers' run of 15 consecutive winning seasons -- the NBA's longest active streak -- will give way to a multiyear run of losing seasons due to the harsh punishments that resulted from the Leonard investigation. Though the Clippers haven't been able to capture a championship, Ballmer had flipped the script from the Clippers' dismal past in which they had a winning record only once between 1992 and 2011. Los Angeles rallied from a terrible start to squeeze out 42 wins last season, but replacing Leonard and James Harden with Brandon Ingram and Darius Garland is bound to cause some regression. The Clippers' longer-term outlook became more complicated when the NBA suspended Ballmer for a year and seized five first-round picks. -- Golliver

Previous ranking: 5

30. Sacramento Kings

Three-year outlook: Sacramento lost 60 games in 2025-26 -- the second most in franchise history -- and now has only one playoff appearance in the past two decades, with a roster that is simultaneously noncompetitive and expensive in the short term. The franchise doesn't appear poised to return to the postseason anytime soon. -- Kram

Roster question looming: Can coach Doug Christie formulate a plan that focuses on player development at the expense of the veterans? The Kings have two distinct timelines: The first is veterans Domantas Sabonis, Malik Monk, Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter. The second is a group of former high draft picks headlined by Darius Acuff Jr. The good news is Sacramento ranks in the top 12 in draft assets and financial flexibility. -- Marks

FPR nugget to know: The gap between Sacramento's total score of 27 and the second-worst team at 34 is the biggest difference we've seen since at least the 2017 version of Future Power Rankings. -- Oliver

Bold prediction for 2027-29: The Kings will have the NBA's worst defense this season (and maybe again in 2027-28). Here's a depressing note: Sacramento hasn't had an above-average defense since 2005-06. During those 20 years, the Kings bottomed out on multiple occasions. They appear headed for another demoralizing campaign after ranking 28th last year. Acuff is bound to be targeted by opposing offenses and Sabonis isn't exactly a stopper. Utah and Washington were the only teams with worse defenses than Sacramento last season, and they both added notable frontcourt upgrades. -- Golliver

Previous ranking: 25

Full team-by-team results

We determined that the most important category is a team's current roster and the future potential of those players. That category accounts for 60% of each NBA team's overall future power rating, the 0-100 score each team receives to determine its overall ranking.

At the same time, we looked at each team's front office and coaching staff (management; 11.67%), future draft assets (draft; 11.67), a team's spending habits and cap situation (money; 11.67%) and the reputation of the city and franchise (market; 5%)

stories.headline: Alexa Grasso shows off flyweight's elite status in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
It's uncommon for two fighters ranked in the pound-for-pound top 10 to meet in a bout with no championship at stake. But that was the case at Saturday's fourth annual Noche UFC, where Alexa Grasso faced Manon Fiorot.

Grasso is a former women's flyweight champion and Fiorot competed for the belt last year, so their status as MMA elites was well established before they fought. And when Grasso won by unanimous decision, she further solidified her standing in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

The top five of the rankings remains intact, and Grasso moves up from 10th to replace Fiorot at No. 6. Fiorot slips two positions to No. 8 in a pound-for-pound hierarchy in which seven of the 10 ranked women compete at flyweight (including Zhang Weili, the former UFC strawweight champion who last fought in an unsuccessful challenge of Valentina Shevchenko in November).

With Shevchenko injured and having vacated her title, there will be much scrambling for the top spot, which will be at stake when No. 5 Natalia Silva fights unranked Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 16. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Alexa Grasso; 6. Manon Fiorot; 7. Dakota Ditcheva; 8. Natalia Silva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Ditcheva; 9. Suarez; 10. Fiorot.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

Other fighters receiving votes: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Ciryl Gane; 7. Tom Aspinall; 8. Arman Tsarukyan; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Alexandre Pantoja.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Justin Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Gane; 8. Joshua Van; 9. Yan; 10. Pantoja.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Pantoja; 6. Gaethje; 7. Topuria; 8. Volkanovski; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Pantoja; 6. Gaethje; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Van.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Pantoja; 4. Yan; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Topuria; 8. Gane; 9. Pereira; 10. Volkanovski.

stories.headline: Max vs 100: Meet the drivers racing against Red Bull's Verstappen
stories.summary: Ahead of Max vs 100, here's single driver competing against Max Verstappen in the event streamed live on Disney+.
stories.body:
Four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen will take on 100 drivers in a unique go-karting event live on ESPN on Disney+ on Sept. 16.

Those competing are a mixture of athletes, content creators, streamers and other personalities from around the world, all with the same goal -- keeping Verstappen behind.

The drivers will be racing around a circuit that has been purpose-built for the occasion.

Here's the confirmed list of drivers taking part so far.

- Max vs 100: F1 superstar Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

- Max vs 100: When is Verstappen race, how to watch on Disney+, how it works, who's taking part?

- What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records

Zac Alsop - YouTuber

Alsop has gone viral for his stunts and social experiments. He's been part of several "sneak-in" videos at events including sneaking past security into MMA star Conor McGregor's dressing room on his 30th birthday.

Tyrique Hyde - Streamer

Known for taking part in the reality television show Love Island UK in 2023 and now regularly live-streams on Twitch.

Queen B (Rebecca Evans) - Motorsport creator and presenter

She might be one to watch out for on the track as she started go-karting at eight years old, before doing drag racing aged 14. She has built a career in car culture and has hosted digital content for Top Gear and featured in Red Bull TV original series Drift Queen.

Pieface23 (Jack McDermott) - Content Creator

He's best known for gaming and football and featured on Big Brother UK in 2015. He's now a full-time streamer on Twitch and streams content related to football and video games.

TGFBro (Romell Henry) - YouTube Content Creator
He's amassed over six million subscribers on YouTube since he started in 2012. His channel has videos involving extreme stunts and wild challenges.

Manny (Emmanuel David Brown) - YouTuber

His content is mainly focused on football and he's got two million followers on YouTube. He's also one of the hosts on the podcast 'Family Ties' which he hosts with his brothers.

Dantic (Daniel Moss) - Content Creator and YouTuber

He posts gaming and travel videos which have gone viral online. His videos on YouTube vary between trying every type of water park, trying different tiers of plane seats and gaming in every single train seat on a journey.

Amber Gill - Personality

She has been on several television shows in the UK, but was launched into the spotlight after she won Love Island in 2019. She has since featured on shows such as Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins.

Stungpegg (Nieve Petruzziello) - Sports Presenter and Content Creator

She's a popular UK content creator, writer, and presenter with a focus on football content with just under 200,000 followers on Instagram.

Bash The Entertainer (Bachala Mbunzama) - Content Creator and Comedian

He's a Scottish social media influencer and is known for his infectious laugh and famous smile. He's worked with brands such as NFL and Adidas and a video made about Rihanna went viral.

Developer Adam (Adam Powell) - Content Creator
Powell focuses his content on gaming, coding and tech and has also posted several videos on motorsport.

Kalia Lai - Content Creator and Athlete
She's an active runner and does boxing with a focus on general fitness content as well.

James Doyle - Creator

He's from Ireland and posts mainly content related to health and entertainment. He's competed in several HYROX events and has travelled the world including visiting Japan.

Drift Games (David Egan) - Creator

Another driver to potentially watch out for is Egan, who competes in drift racing and also has a YouTube channel that shows you what he gets up to.

GoKartGod - Manufacturer of Electric Go-Karts

The Instagram account is full of content following the next generation of go-karts.

Larry Chen - Photographer

Based in America, he's a car photographer and has over one million followers on Instagram.

Neo Yau (Yau Hawk Sau) - Actor

He's an actor, writer and digital content creator from Hong Kong.

Mike Dokas

His TikTok channel mainly focuses on football and Formula 1 content. He has over 350,000 followers on the platform.

AustrianKiwi (Jonathan Balchin) - Comedian

He makes funny and relatable videos around daily life in Austria.

Nathan Lust - Creator

He's from New Zealand but lives in Australia and has over one million followers on Instagram. His videos are based on comedy including filming behind the scenes on the Avengers and references to Toy Story.

Tettrem (Mateus dos Santos Machado Almeida) - Content creator and co-founder of POV Creators

He's a digital content creator, streamer from Brazil and blew up through viral reaction videos. He has nearly 12 million followers on Instagram.

Mars (Zhang Jing ) - Chinese key opinion leader in extreme sports

From China, his content online features lots of cars and car culture.

Pamkutya (Norbert Osbath) - Content Creator

Osbáth Norbert is a prominent Hungarian content creator, traveler, and author, best known as one-half of PamKutya which he co-founded in 2010.

Roberts Vītols - Content Creator

He's a content creator from Latvia who focuses on cars and culture.

Paky TWC (Patrick Tremolada) - YouTuber

A YouTuber from Italy, he focuses on cool car tricks and has over a million followers on Instagram.

Enis Kirazoğlu - Content Creator

From Türkiye, his content mainly focuses on gaming and he has over 1 million followers on YouTube.

Karol Zdęba - YouTuber

His content is based around adventures with videos including heading to abandoned towns and staying there for several days.

Vale Sulca - Content Creator

Based in the LATAM region, she has half a million followers on Instagram and mainly shares her adventures and lifestyle.

German Rodezel - Content Creator

He's also based in the LATAM region and enjoys making videos and has a passion for music and Formula 1.

Pableke (Pablo Jimenez) - Content Creator

From Chile, his content mainly focuses on motorsport and he has half a million followers on Instagram.

Josh Richards - Creator and Entrepreneur
He's from Canada and is an internet star who rose to fame on TikTok. He's also an entrepreneur and has set up several brands.

Si Hyun Park - Professional Drift Driver

Another one to watch out for, based in South Korea, is a karting driver who focuses on drifting with over one million followers on Instagram.

John-Marc van Wyk - Content Creator

The South African has half a million followers on Instagram and posts lifestyle content.

Dyler - Content Creator

He's a Saudi Arabian artist and content creator with a following of nearly four million people.

Nnnurdaylet - Content Creator

He does a whole heap of different videos and has a huge following of over five million people.

Julia Haller (Julia Alzire Elisabeth Haller) - Content Creator

She posts lifestyle and motorsport content with over 600,000 followers on Instagram.

Wirtual (Øyvind Ludwig Iversen) - Content Creator
He makes videos on Trackmania which is the world's most competitive racing game.

Daniel Ahola - Content Creator

His content features lots of adventures around the world, usually with little to no money.

Gabs Djay - Motorsport Content Creator

She focuses on motorsport news, particularly Formula 1, along with other sports such as football.

Joe Tasker - Content Creator and TV Presenter

He posts comedy videos that most people will be able to relate to and has over 900,000 followers on TikTok.

Bella James - Content Creator

Lots of her content is based around drivers in motorsport, famously interviewing team principals with dry humour.

Juank Perez - Content Creator

Juank is a prominent Latin American sports digital content creator, social media influencer, and digital host for ESPN México.

Fresia Aria - Football Reporter

She's a sports journalist and presenter who has worked for ESPN Netherlands since 2018. Aria covers mainly Dutch football in the Eredivisie.

Nate Saunders - F1 Sports Reporter

Saunders has covered Formula 1 for ESPN since 2014 and has attended races all over the globe, and has interviewed Max Verstappen himself on many occasions.

Jakidale (Jacopo D'Alesio) - YouTuber and Content Creator

He's an Italian YouTuber and creator who makes content on technology, travel and science, with over 600,000 followers on Instagram.

Sporttouchen (Timothé Rangström) - Content Creator
He's a Swedish creator who founded digital sport media company Sporttouchen which is best known for football content aimed at younger audiences.

Bea Eguiraun - Motorsport Content Creator
Eguiraun is a Spanish motorcycle presenter and test rider. She began working professionally in motorsport in 2014 with Dorna Sports, creating social media content and working around MotoGP broadcasts, before going on to present the TV show Locos por las Motos.

TheGrefg - Streamer and Content Creator

He's one of Spain's biggest gaming creators and is particularly known for Fortnite with 12.29 million followers on Twitch and 19.9 million followers on YouTube. In 2021, more than 2.4 million people tuned in to the reveal of his Fortnite skin, which set a Guinness World Record for concurrent viewers on an individual Twitch stream at the time.

Caedrel (Marc Lamont) - Streamer

Lamont is a former professional League of Legends player who moved into League of Legends European Championship (LEC) casting and analytics before becoming a full-time streamer. In 2024, he founded esports organisation Los Ratones and has become one of the biggest personalities in the LoL community.

TheDonato (Donato José Muñoz Calabres) - Streamer and Content Creator

TheDonato is a Venezuelan Red Bull partnered gaming creator who built a huge following through games including Garena Free Fire. He has more than 40 million subscribers on YouTube, with the creator himself crediting his switch to Free Fire as a major turning point in his career.

Helydia (Celia Tansel) - Streamer and Content Creator

Helydia is a French Valorant player and streamer who has built her community through competitive gaming content on Twitch and YouTube. She's also a Red Bull player and regularly takes part in Valorant showmatches and gaming events.

Diogo 'MoveMind' da Silva - Streamer and Content Creator

MoveMind is one of Portugal's best-known streamers and started broadcasting on Twitch as a hobby in 2017. He first broke through while commentating on matches involving professional Portuguese FIFA players and has since made the transition from reporting on esports and virtual FIFA matches to live sports broadcasting of real football games.

Jonathan Amaral - Professional Esports Player

Better known as Jonathan Gaming, Amaral is one of India's leading mobile esports players and is best known for competing in BGMI and PUBG Mobile. In 2026, he launched his own esports organisation, Team Apex Gaming.

RDJavi (Steven Javier Santos del Rosario) - Streamer

RDJavi is a Dominican streamer and gaming YouTuber known widely for his gaming content, particularly GTA V, GTA Roleplay, and automotive vlogs.

TechnoGamerz - Gaming Content Creator

Ujjwal Chaurasia, better known as Techno Gamerz, is one of India's biggest gaming creators and is particularly known for his GTA V content. In 2026, he became the first individual gaming creator in India and all of Asia to pass 50 million subscribers on YouTube.

Amar - Streamer and Entertainer

Amar Al-Naimi, better known as AmarCoDTV, is one of the leading figures in Germany's streaming scene, with content centred around gaming and entertainment. His background includes competitive Call of Duty, while Fortnite has also become a major part of his streaming career.

Nugato - Streamer

Ilija 'Nugato' Ravlić is a Croatian gamer and YouTuber who started creating content in 2013. He became particularly known for Minecraft videos and is now part of Red Bull's gaming roster.

iiTzTimmy (Timothy An) - Streamer

Timothy An, better known as iiTzTimmy, is an American streamer and professional Apex Legends competitor. He's known for marathon gaming challenges, including a Solo Bronze to Predator 34-hour stream that went viral where he went from Rookie to Predator in 126 games.

Qucee (Quentin Correia) - Streamer

Qucee is a Dutch YouTuber, rapper and streamer who is also part of the Supergaande collective. His content has included comedy, street interviews, freestyle rap and live-streaming.

Leticia Bufoni - Professional Skateboarder

Bufoni is a six-time X Games gold medallist, a former world No. 1 and 2015 SLS Super Crown Champion. She holds multiple Guinness World Records and represented Brazil at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics. From go-karting in her youth she's since added motor racing to her résumé and competes in Porsche Cup Brazil, so she could be one to watch on the track.

Sarah Vignot Lezito - Stunt Rider

Sarah Vignot, known professionally as Sarah Lezito is a world-famous French motorcycle stunt rider who began practising her craft as a teenager. Her riding skills have also taken her to Hollywood, where she has performed motorcycle stunt work in major films as a movie stunt double.

Arda Saatçi - Ultra Athlete

Known as 'Cyborg', Saatçi is a German-Turkish extreme endurance athlete and Red Bull Athlete who specialises in extreme endurance challenges. He initially wanted to become a professional footballer, playing for Berliner AK U19 and SV Altlüdersdorf in his youth before injury led him towards endurance sport.

Lethal Shooter (Chris Matthews) - NBA Shooting Coach

Matthews is a former professional basketball player and Red Bull partner who is now one of the sport's most sought-after shooting coaches. Known as 'Lethal Shooter', he's worked with players from both the NBA and WNBA to improve their shooting.

Janja Garnbret - Professional Climber

Garnbret is widely regarded as one of the greatest competition climbers of all time. The Slovenian is a two-time Olympic champion, has won 10 world titles and over 50 World Cup gold medals. In 2026 she recorded her 50th World Cup victory.

Leo Neugebauer - Decathlon World Champion

Neugebauer is a German track and field athlete who won the decathlon world title for Germany in Tokyo in 2025 after previously taking silver at the Paris Olympics. He holds the German national records for both the outdoor decathlon (8,961 points) and the indoor heptathlon as well as taking the men's decathlon title at the Birmingham 2026 European Athletics Championships.

Molly Carlson - Professional Cliff Diver

Carlson is a Canadian high diver, Red Bull cliff diving athlete and a three-time World Championship silver medalist (2022, 2023, and 2024). She's also built a huge online community through her #BraveGang movement to encourage self-love, body positivity, and overcoming fears.

Matt Jones (Matthew Jones) - Red Bull MTB Athlete

Jones is a professional British mountain bike (MTB) freeride and slopestyle athlete. He broke onto the international scene in 2013 and has become known for pushing the limits of the sport with innovative tricks and riding projects.

Billy Bolt - Motorcycle Racer

Bolt should certainly be comfortable with speed as he's a world-renowned, six-time FIM SuperEnduro world champion. The British rider also won the inaugural FIM Hard Enduro World Championship in 2021.

Aidan Heslop - Cliff Diver

Heslop is a British-Welsh high diver who won the men's 27m world title in 2024 at the World Aquatics Championships in Doha. That same year, he was crowned Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series champion after winning four stops during the season.

Pol Tarrés - Enduro Rider

Tarrés is a Spanish trials, hard enduro and rally raid rider who has become known for doing extraordinary things on a Yamaha Ténéré 700. He won the 2024 Morocco Desert Challenge and also set a world record by reaching an altitude of 6,756 metres on a twin-cylinder motorcycle.

Tommo McCluskey - Content Creator

McCluskey, better known online as just Tommo, is a British Formula 1 content creator, presenter and podcaster. He has over 341,000 subscribers on his YouTube channel where he uploads deep dives, quizzes and analysis videos.

Taylor Serage - Content Creator

Taylor Serage is a New Zealand social-media personality and former real-estate agent who has become known for combining fashion, cars, property and lifestyle content on social media. She has over 747,000 followers on Instagram.

Joseph Brophy - TalkSPORT writer

A sports journalist and SEO writer at talkSPORT, specialising in producing digital sports content. He has written extensively across football and other major sporting events.

Supercar Blondie (Niklaus Manuel Hirschi) - CEO and co-founder of Supercar Blondie

Co-founder, along with his wife Alex Hirschi, and CEO of Supercar Blondie, a global automotive media empire. They have over 17 million followers on Instagram and showcase videos of cars, tech and luxury around the world.

Shreeman Legend (Siddhant Praveen Joshi) - Streamer and YouTuber

An Indian gaming content creator and streamer best known for his PUBG Mobile/BGMI content. He became one of India's prominent gaming creators through his energetic gameplay videos and his distinctive blend of Marathi and Hindi commentary.

Shredded Fox (Jan Liška) - YouTuber

A Czech fitness influencer, YouTuber, entrepreneur and former professional online fitness coach. He has spent around a decade in the fitness industry, building a large online following through content about training, nutrition, healthy living and his own fitness journey. He is the only Czech participant in the race.

Molly Marsh - Influencer

A British influencer, musical-theatre performer and television personality, best known for appearing on Love Island series 10 in 2023, where she finished fourth alongside Zachariah Noble.

Mélanie Buffetaud - Content Creator

Buffetaud is a French content creator, filmmaker and parkour athlete. Her content focuses heavily on sport, physical challenges, adventure and pushing the limits. Alongside her partner Charles Poujade, she has built an audience of more than three million subscribers.

Jojo Sim - Content Creator

Jojo Sim is an American social media content creator who makes videos of everything from off-road driving to NASCAR-related content.

MrCarSounds (Greg Gevojanyan) - Content Creator

An American content creator best known for his extraordinary ability to mimic car and engine sounds using his voice. His videos feature everything from supercars and racing cars to trucks and motorcycles, and he has built millions of followers across social media.

ExtraEmily (Emily Xuechun Zhang) - Streamer

Known for her high-energy IRL streams, gaming, challenges and comedic content, Extra Emily is an American Twitch streamer who graduated magna cum laude from Columbia University with a degree in Financial Engineering before pursuing streaming full-time.

Henry Robert Williams (Daily Mail) - Journalist

A British sports presenter and social-media journalist at the Daily Mail, who has said it was his dream to be a sports presenter since the age of 12.

Charles Poujade - Parkour Athlete and Content Creator

Poujade was part of the French team called United that won the 2019 World Chase Tag Championship. He is also a social media creator with a YouTube audience of more than three million.

Austin Sprinz - YouTuber and Content Creator

Austin Sprinz is an American TikTok and YouTube creator from Arizona known for comedy, challenges, experiments and lifestyle content. He has made content across a range of sports including NASCAR, F1, UFC and the Winter Olympics.

Stream Max vs 100 globally on ESPN on Disney+ on Wednesday, Sept. 16. Coverage starts at 5 p.m. BST, before the race begins at 6 p.m.

stories.summary: Washington Mystics (24-16, 11-5 Eastern Conference) at Chicago Sky (15-25, 3-13 Eastern Conference)
stories.body:
Washington Mystics (24-16, 11-5 Eastern Conference) at Chicago Sky (15-25, 3-13 Eastern Conference)

Chicago; Thursday, 8 p.m. EDT

LINE: Mystics -3.5; over/under is 167.5

BOTTOM LINE: Washington Mystics plays the Chicago Sky after Sonia Citron scored 22 points in the Mystics' 88-82 loss to the Los Angeles Sparks.

The Sky have gone 3-13 against Eastern Conference teams. Chicago ranks third in the Eastern Conference with 41.7 points per game in the paint led by Kamilla Cardoso averaging 11.1.

The Mystics are 11-5 in Eastern Conference play. Washington ranks sixth in the Eastern Conference with 19.6 assists per game led by Citron averaging 4.3.

Chicago is shooting 44.1% from the field this season, 0.9 percentage points higher than the 43.2% Washington allows to opponents. Washington averages 82.8 points per game, 6.9 fewer points than the 89.7 Chicago allows to opponents.

The teams square off for the second time this season. The Mystics won 90-72 in the last meeting on June 2. Shakira Austin led the Mystics with 17 points, and Sydney Taylor led the Sky with 15 points.

TOP PERFORMERS: Cardoso is averaging 14.8 points, 8.7 rebounds and 1.5 blocks for the Sky. Natasha Cloud is averaging 15.3 points over the last 10 games.

stories.headline: Cristian 'Kily' González arrives to take charge of Messi, Miami
stories.summary: New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.
stories.body:
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. -- New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.

González has now received the authorization to begin the job after being announced last month as the permanent replacement for interim coach Guillermo Hoyos on a contract through June 2028.

- Source: Colombia targeting U.S. U20 dual national Shaw

- Messi tracker: All goals, assists, key moments for Miami, Argentina in 2026

- Messi scores, but Nashville strikes late to deny Miami win

The job sees him reunite with Messi after the two shared the field for Argentina in two World Cup qualifiers in 2005.

"There are things in football that simply cannot be described in words; they are unique feelings. I feel privileged and blessed to have this opportunity and to share the fantastic relationship I have with Leo," González said in a news conference.

"I adore him, he knows it, and that makes this moment even more special. Being with him and sharing experiences with the incredible players on this squad. Honestly, as a coach, I feel completely fulfilled.

"Of course, this is all wonderful, but now we have to get to work. God willing, we'll start off strong tomorrow and win the championship."

González led his first training session with Inter Miami on Tuesday after landing in Miami from Argentina earlier in the morning. He will be on the sidelines for the team's Campeones Cup match against Liga MX champions Cruz Azul on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.

Inter Miami reached an agreement with González on Aug. 27, but the coach could not take over for Hoyos until receiving his work permit.

"What were these past few days like? To be honest, they were filled with a lot of anticipation. It had been nearly two and a half weeks and I couldn't be here, but this unique opportunity, something I hadn't even dared to dream of, became a reality," González said.

"We spoke with the club, and they offered me the chance to join the team; I said yes immediately. Being with the players, seeing their willingness to welcome my coaching staff, and watching them train the way they did today honestly, it made me very happy and gave me a huge boost of energy for tomorrow's match."

Miami's opponent in the Campeones Cup was delayed in arriving in Miami for the game and instead of landing in the U.S. on Monday, were unable to fly in until Tuesday.

"Well, more than an odyssey, sometimes accidents like this happen, and you just have to turn the page," said Cruz Azul manager Joel Huiqui. "The team is doing well. We rested very well yesterday, we stayed at a hotel in Mexico, and we're just arriving now. We're calm, obviously aware that tomorrow will be a huge match for us, and we're all focused.

"It goes without saying that [Messis] is a great player, but what matters most to me is that the team realizes what is at stake: not just another trophy, but our consolidation as an institution. Beyond the chance to face a great player, the opportunity to win the title against a team like Inter Miami is about solidifying the work we've been doing and, above all, bringing joy to the fans."

Inter Miami currently sits in second place on the Eastern Conference table with 45 points in 25 games. The team has recorded just one victory in its last nine games.

Inter Miami forward Luis Suárez said he wants to use the game against Cruz Azul to start strong under new leadership.

"When it comes to playing a match like this, it's a final. There is no time to dwell on the past, the only thing that matters is looking ahead to tomorrow," Suárez said. "We've come through a challenging run of games, but now we face the best possible scenario: playing a final and moving forward with a new coach who brings great positive energy, a strong desire to grow and plenty of enthusiasm.

"That attitude is contagious, and we are ready to support him and his coaching staff."

Inter Miami hosts Cruz Azul before returning to Major League Soccer regular season action on Sunday against San Diego.

stories.headline: Warriors sell out Eden Park in 48 hours amid NRL's crowd woes
stories.summary: Hooker Sam Healey plans to draw inspiration from his rugby league idol to help him handle the pulsating atmosphere of a sold-out Eden Park.
stories.body:
Hooker Sam Healey plans to draw inspiration from his NRL idol to help him handle the pulsating atmosphere of a sold-out Eden Park.

The NRL announced that general-public tickets for Sunday's do-or-die semi-final between the Warriors and Newcastle in Auckland had sold out in less than 48 hours.

It comes after New Zealand were forced to relocate from their traditional home ground for the clash because Eden Park hosts about 25,000 more spectators than Go Media Stadium.

The 50,000-seat venue being full comes after the league was criticised over poor crowd numbers in the first week of finals, although the Warriors had a mostly sold-out attendance for their 26-16 loss to the Dolphins.

Regardless, it's the club's first clash at Eden Park since 2014, and will be a mammoth moment for New Zealand rugby league as the Warriors look to keep alive their hopes of a first premiership.

Healey is yet to play at the venue, but will be wanting to produce similar heroics to his idol Kevin Locke, who made a courageous try-saving tackle on Sydney Roosters centre Michael Jennings at the Fortress in 2013.

"I have played league since I was five or six or something like that, so I always loved the game," Healey said.

"I actually saw him (Locke) in the sheds the other day, and I said to my mum, 'Do you remember when he was my favourite player'. She just started laughing.

"He used to be my lock-screen on my phone ... I just said g'day."

Warriors back-rower Jacob Laban has only played once at the country's biggest sporting stadium.

"It was Kiwi A's versus Tonga A's, I think it was two, three years ago," he said.

"(After) New Zealand played Samoa (in the Pacific Championships) ... it was a pretty cool, good atmosphere.

"Obviously it (the crowd) is a little bit further (away) than Mt Smart, but it's not too bad. When you score a try, you can walk up to the fans over there, so it's still pretty close."

Laban won't be intimidated by the history of Eden Park, although the club has won only one of its six games at the venue.

The blond second-rower is intent on not just helping the Warriors set up a preliminary final against Penrith, but also on making his childhood self proud.

"I knew I wanted to play for the Warriors when I first heard about rugby league," Laban said.

"They came to Wellington. I don't know what year it was, but I still have this photo of me where I had half a Warriors face painted on and a Warriors T-shirt.

"I knew I wanted to play for the Warriors since I was young."

stories.headline: Start here before you draft your fantasy hockey goalie: Best picks from early to late
stories.summary: From the starters, to the sleepers and the timeshares, here's a guide to the fantasy hockey goalie position.
stories.body:
Responsible for too many categories carrying too much weight, these characters play too great a part in determining your fantasy teams' success (or failure) to tackle lightly. Never even mind the extra influence brought on by negative figures that detract from your team's overall total. You won't win your league with sub-par goaltending, that's all there is to it.

To illustrate, sticking with my perennial example from ESPN's standard game, a goalie who stops 28 of 30 shots in a 4-2 win produces 5.6 prized points. While surrendering five goals on 31 shots in a 5-4 loss nets a loss of -4.8 points. There's no worse feeling than watching your own fantasy netminder hemorrhage digits in real time while their coach leaves them out to dry. Especially when such a swing means the difference between winning your week or not. It's going to happen. The key is to secure the candidates that fall victim to such scenarios far less often.

In standard redraft competition, the winning formula doesn't waver: You want a fantasy goalie who plays as much as possible for a better than average team, while denying the largest conceivable percentage of shots-faced. The challenge, of course, is to suss out who fits that fantasy mold in the here and now. As much as we can appreciate the individual prowess of a Dustin Wolf or John Gibson or Spencer Knight, if the club is going to struggle as a whole, fantasy points will always be harder to come by.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

Strategy

In deeper conventional leagues comprising 10-12 managers, you're advised to corral your top-two netminders early on, then pad your roster with high-ceilinged sleepers or others in position to exceed expectations. If they work out, great. If not, you can later sub them out for those who overachieve their way out of the goaltending woodwork. Guaranteed, there weren't many who had Brandon Bussi, Dan Vadar, or Jakub Dobes in their fantasy sights ahead of 2025-26. Yet all three ended up rewarding their managers handsomely.

The Hellebuyck Issue

As of mid-September, and despite his publicized wishes to be elsewhere, Connor Hellebuyck remains a member of the Winnipeg Jets. You can count on that being the case until GM Kevin Cheveldayoff receives an offer for his elite goaltender he finds sufficiently palatable. But while it isn't possible to thoroughly assess Hellebuyck without knowing where he's going to end up (hopefully) sooner rather than later, and last year's anomalously poor showing notwithstanding, he's too gifted not to target. Plus, if you're worried about the 2025 Hart/Vezina Trophy winner not showing up to compete for the Jets to start 2026-27, current scuttlebutt suggests he remains committed to being a good teammate until matters are resolved. Grab him after he's bypassed a couple of times by those more squeamish.

Elite goalies to target

Andrei Vasilevskiy, Tampa Bay Lightning: (projected: 171.4, last season: 172.6)

Plays for a great team? Check. More active than just about anyone else? Check. Remarkable personal and team (wins) stats? Also check. Durable? Allowing for a two-month absence to start 2023 because of a disc issue, there's another bold tick mark. If you're going to exercise the option of selecting a goaltender exceptionally early, Tampa's No. 1 is your guy.

Top-tier goalies to target

Logan Thompson, Washington Capitals: (projected: 136.8, last season: 151.4)

We should probably get used to the idea that the former Golden Knight is now a top echelon fantasy netminder in Washington. He certainly performed as such this past season, finishing third in points in ESPN standard leagues. Plus, one the busiest clubs this offseason, the Capitals are perceivably better out front of the underrated netminder with Alex Tuch, Jordan Kyrou, and Boone Jenner aboard. Alex Ovechkin isn't returning for another go around just to hang in there. Once Vasilevskiy is off the board, Thompson is my top fantasy choice between the pipes.

Secondary top-tier goalies to target

Jake Oettinger, Dallas Stars: (projected: 132.2, last season: 128.8)

While not exactly the "Rodney Dangerfield" of the fantasy crease, the Stars' go-to netminder still doesn't quite get the respect he deserves. Since truly taking over in 2021-22, Oettinger has a 173-70-26 record for a very good Dallas team. Only Vasilevskiy has more victories in that stretch (seven), in 20 more games. Sure, sometimes the individual integers don't sparkle as much as they do for others, and yes, he's going to stumble through a couple (or more) mediocre stretches over the course of a regular season. That's why you pad your roster with other goalies to pick up the slack, when necessary. In ESPN standard and similar leagues, Oettinger serves as a top-5 fantasy netminder.

Ilya Sorokin, New York Islanders: (projected: 109.6, last season: 128.2)

Competing for a superior squad, Sorokin would present as a top-tier fantasy goalie, no question. As it stands though, the reigning Vezina nominee plays for a very middle-of-the-pack-at-best Islanders team in a tough Metropolitan division, and even tougher Eastern Conference, when considering the strength of the Atlantic. The injection of new head coach Pete DeBoer, who took over for Patrick Roy in early April, is interesting though. As is the prospect of this squad taking another step forward with young star Matthew Schaefer entering his second season. If the Isles can manage to rifle the puck in the net steadily enough -- an enduring concern -- Sorokin will serve as one of the best in the fantasy biz. Even though other netminders on better teams will carve out more victories, when all is said and done.

Karel Vejmelka, Utah Mammoth: (projected: 121.4, last season: 114.6)

The only netminder to bust through the 60-mark, as no one made more starts (63) for their team in 2025-26. As long as GM Bill Armstrong doesn't fiddle with his goalie corps that now also includes former Detroit prospect Sebastian Cossa, Vejmelka will be right up there again this round, challenging Vasilevskiy for most wins. I'd also argue that after making the postseason this past campaign, the Mammoth are even stronger with forwards Vincent Trocheck and Anders Lee aboard, and defender MacKenzie Weegar in place for the entire season.

See also:

Igor Shesterkin, New York Rangers: (projected: 104.0, last season: 116.6)

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

Mid-tier goalies to target

Jeremy Swayman, Boston Bruins: (projected: 117.0, last season: 127.2)

Yes, I'm well aware the Bruins goalie performed beyond admirably in what can only be characterized as one of the most impressive comeback performances of 2025-26. He was outstanding. However, I'm still looking at this Boston roster and wondering how it's going to measure up against all the other monsters in the Atlantic. The Panthers are apparently back. Tampa Bay remains strong. The Montreal Canadiens and Buffalo Sabres appear legit. The Ottawa Senators and Toronto Maple Leafs can't be disregarded. Wins will be hard to come by from a club that can expect regular production from David Pastrnak, maybe newbie JJ Peterka, perhaps Morgan Geekie and Pavel Zacha, and that's about it. Individually, Swayman will have to be that much better than other fantasy goaltenders on superior teams.

See also:

Linus Ullmark, Ottawa Senators: (projected: 107.0, last season: 80.4)
Jakub Dobes, Montreal Canadiens: (projected: 100.0, last season: 90.6)

Tandem teammates to target

Brandon Bussi, Carolina Hurricanes: (projected: 110.2, last season: 101.2)

Are we so sure Pyotr Kochetkov is going to see a healthy amount of playing time for the Hurricanes in 2026-27? After contributing nada to his club's first Cup in 20 years, I'm not convinced as much. In fact, the greater threat to Bussi's fantasy value may be the prospect of GM Eric Tulsky acquiring another prominent netminder before the season is through. Which isn't out of the question. Otherwise, Bussi projects to compete a whole lot for plausibly the best team in the East.

Sergei Bobrovsky, Toronto Maple Leafs: (projected: 67.8, last season: 32.2)

The Maple Leafs aren't paying the two-time Stanley Cup Champ $7-million to share the load equally with Anthony Stolarz. Bobrovsky will start a minimum of 50 games for a Toronto team that looks a lot better since snatching defender Darren Raddysh, a gaggle of scrappy depth forwards, and top-draft pick Gavin McKenna.

Key sleepers

Jet Greaves, Columbus Blue Jackets: (projected: 77.4, last season: 114.4)

The young netminder in Columbus is already garnering much attention as one-to-watch in what's expected to be his first full season, I wonder if he still qualifies as a true sleeper. Regardless, with Elvis Merzlikins hurt, and just-signed Cam Talbot in place to contribute sporadically at 39 years old, the Jackets' net belongs to the 25-year-old. If this squad remains competitive enough under Rick Bowness -- hey, Zach Werenski and Kirill Marchenko are still there -- Greaves will put up solid fantasy numbers.

Stuart Skinner, Winnipeg Jets: (projected: 49.2, last season: 48.0)

If Cheveldayoff manages to trade Hellebuyck in the not-too-distant and doesn't get a true heavy hitter in net in return, and the Jets perform much better than whatever that was this past season, Skinner could prove a pleasant fantasy surprise 2026-27. A lot of ifs there, sure, but the 27-year-old has been to two Stanley Cup Finals in the past three years. He's worth a flyer late in drafts as a potentially sneaky fantasy performer.

See also:

Juuse Saros, Nashville Predators: (projected: 74.2, last season: 61.8)

Late-round picks to consider

Jacob Markstrom, Florida Panthers: (projected: 63.0, last season: 32.6)

A fiddle-fit Aleksander Barkov is back, as is defender Radko Gudas, after a three-year stint in Anaheim. Veteran depth center Lars Eller and pest Garnet Hathaway are now part of the Florida fold. Oh, and then there's that Brady Tkachuk who's intensely jazzed to compete with his brother Matthew after bolting from Ottawa. After a banged-up off year, the Panthers are once again poised to make a great deal of noise in an anticipated march to the postseason. If Markstrom can hold down his end of the bargain in his second Florida turn -- as he has in previous stints with the Vancouver Canucks, Calgary Flames, and New Jersey Devils -- the 36-year-old could end up serving as one of the league's most valuable fantasy netminders. Keep in mind, the organization picked this guy to replace Bobrovsky -- not Akira Schmid.

See also:

Darcy Kuemper, Los Angeles Kings: (projected: 74.6, last season: 52.0)

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Avoid in drafts at current value

Scott Wedgewood, Colorado Avalanche: (projected: 140.6, last season: 171.4)

I'm not entirely sure why we're expecting the 34-year-old to once more put up similarly flashy fantasy numbers when Mackenzie Blackwood is starting the season healthy. Barring another injury to Colorado's other netminder, Wedgewood stands to split starts fairly even-stevens. Another serving of 16 measly regulation losses for the Avs is also a big ask. While the veteran is more than a serviceable fantasy performer in most leagues, there are too many other clear No. 1 netminders to target first.

Joel Hofer, St. Louis Blues (projected: 110.0, last season: 118.4)

At last check, Jordan Binnington was still a member of the Blues. As such, the 33-year-old can still be expected to pitch in his fair share of starts for an okay-but-not-great hockey club in a robustly competitive Central division. Top-20 fantasy netminder? Sure. But it's a stretch to expect Hofer to put up top-10 numbers in his contemporary role with his current team.

See also:

Filip Gustavsson, Minnesota Wild: (projected: 131.2, last season: 113.0)
